articles.title: Strategic Evaluation of Planning Strategies for LLM Agents in Cyber-Physical Systems
articles.summary: The paper introduces a physics-grounded benchmark for evaluating LLM planning agents in cyber-physical systems, using a smart-grid demand-response setting with 40 heterogeneous prosumers and an independently simulated radial feeder. Results suggest planning architecture materially affects outcomes, and that feasibility checks are critical because mode agreement alone can hide operational failures such as increased voltage shortfall.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is an early-stage technical development rather than a direct commercial deployment, but it highlights an important adoption hurdle for AI agents in physical infrastructure: successful task completion or plan adherence is not enough when autonomous participants and physics-constrained systems interact. For advisors, the read-through is that AI adoption in grids, industrial operations, and other cyber-physical settings may require rigorous simulation, feasibility validation, and governance layers before broad deployment.
